Audit the Markdown document's Python code blocks and headings, by these rules, a small fixed subset of CommonMark:
- A fence is a line of three or more backticks or tildes, indented by at most three spaces. A backtick fence's info text may not contain a backtick.
- A block is Python when the first word of its info text is python, in any case. Other fences are skipped whole, so nothing inside them counts.
- A fence closes at a line of the same character, at least as long, with nothing after it. A block that is never closed runs to the end of the document and is reported with closed false.
- The block's code is the lines between the fences, each with up to the opening fence's indent removed, joined by a newline. line is the opening fence's line number from 1. index is the block's position among the Python blocks, from 0.
- A heading is an ATX heading outside any fence: one to six # characters, then a space or tab, then non-blank text, with an optional closing run of #. Setext headings are not recognised. level is the number of # characters, title the text without them and without the closing #s, and line its line number from 1.
- A \r\n and a lone \r each count as a line end.
Every block is reported, valid or not: valid says whether its code parses as Python (use Python's own ast), and error says why not, or is an empty string when it does. all_valid is true when every block is closed and valid, which includes a document with no blocks.
